headline: Salt Lake City called a 'lock' for MLB expansion as Nashville leads in the East
summary: USA Today MLB insider Bob Nightengale labeled Salt Lake City a 'lock' to land one of MLB's two planned expansion franchises, with Nashville viewed as the frontrunner in the East. MLB aims to grow from 30 to 32 teams, though Commissioner Rob Manfred has said the process won't begin in earnest until the Athletics' and Rays' stadium situations are resolved, with new teams unlikely to play before the early 2030s.

headline: Record $3.9B Padres sale to Feliciano and Jones gets initial MLB approval
summary: MLB's ownership committee gave initial approval to the sale of the San Diego Padres to Clearlake Capital co-founder Jose E. Feliciano and his wife Kwanza Jones for an MLB-record $3.9 billion, shattering the $2.42 billion mark set by Steve Cohen's 2020 Mets purchase. Feliciano, a Chelsea FC co-owner, would become the first Puerto Rican control owner of an MLB club, and Jones the first Black woman with majority ownership of a team. The Seidler family put the club up for sale in November 2025, and Feliciano's group beat out bids led by Dan Friedkin and Warriors owner Joe Lacob.

headline: Tampa City Council divided on next steps for Rays' $2.3B ballpark plan
summary: A week after blocking a key land-use transmittal, Tampa City Council members remained split on how to proceed with the Rays' proposed $2.3 billion stadium and mixed-use district at Hillsborough College's Dale Mabry campus. The impasse clouds the timeline for new owner Patrick Zalupski's goal of opening a Tampa ballpark by 2029, even though Hillsborough County has already approved the nonbinding deal that includes roughly $967 million in public money.

headline: A's file permits for six-story parking garage and utility plant at Vegas ballpark site
summary: The Athletics submitted building-permit applications to Clark County for a six-story parking garage and a central utility plant at their $2 billion Las Vegas ballpark site at Las Vegas Boulevard and Tropicana Avenue. The team is footing the bill for the infrastructure, and county permitting work keeps the 33,000-seat stadium on track for its targeted completion by February 2028.

headline: Tampa council vote stalls Rays stadium land-use step
summary: The Tampa City Council voted 4-3 against transmitting a major land-use amendment for the Rays' $2.3 billion ballpark and mixed-use development to Florida Commerce for state review. The vote did not kill the project or end negotiations, but it halted an administrative step local officials had hoped to clear in mid-July, injecting new uncertainty into the push to open a new Tampa ballpark for the 2029 season.

headline: MLBPA counters MLB's draft overhaul, proposes June draft and tradeable picks
summary: The players union delivered its amateur draft proposal in CBA talks, pushing back on MLB's sweeping overhaul by keeping the 20-round format and high school and junior college eligibility while expanding eligibility to all college sophomores. The MLBPA also proposed moving the draft back to June, allowing trades of picks in the first 10 rounds, and softening bonus-pool penalties so clubs could outspend allotments by up to 15% before forfeiting picks.

headline: Second roof truss rises at A's $2B Las Vegas ballpark
summary: Crews began installing the second of seven steel roof-truss arches at the Athletics' Las Vegas ballpark, a construction milestone for the $2 billion, 33,000-seat venue at the former Tropicana site. The stadium, which will feature a 400-foot-wide glass outfield wall facing the Strip, remains on schedule for completion by February 2028 ahead of the team's relocation from Sacramento.

headline: MLB escalates 'Level the Playing Field' PR war over salary cap
summary: MLB intensified its public campaign for a salary cap, running 'Level the Playing Field' ads during game broadcasts and on MLB.TV and publishing fact sheets arguing payroll disparity is hurting competitive balance. The league is seeking a 2027 hard cap of $245.3 million with a $171.2 million floor; the MLBPA counters that the luxury-tax system works but is misused by owners who pocket revenue sharing, and has floated a 'Competitive Integrity Tax' aimed at low-spending clubs instead.

headline: Netflix's first Home Run Derby draws 5.3M viewers, lowest since 2003
summary: Netflix's debut Home Run Derby broadcast from Philadelphia averaged 5.3 million viewers, down about 7.5% from ESPN's 5.73 million in 2025 and the event's smallest audience in more than two decades. Netflix, which pays roughly $50 million a year in its three-year MLB deal, touted qualitative wins: the youngest Derby audience since 2014 with a median viewer age of 44.3 and the event's best ratings in the 18-34 and 18-49 demos.

headline: Clark blasts MLB's in-broadcast salary cap ads as 'perverse' at All-Star break
summary: Speaking to the Baseball Writers' Association of America before the All-Star Game in Philadelphia, MLBPA executive director Tony Clark condemned MLB's salary-cap ad campaign, saying 'a cap is not about a partnership' and is instead about franchise values and profits. Commissioner Rob Manfred, in his own session, defended the league's push and did not rule out a lockout when the CBA expires December 1, deepening expectations of a work stoppage that could threaten the 2027 season.

headline: MLBPA fires back with CBA package on roster rules and data transparency
summary: Less than a week after MLB's salary-cap proposal, the players union delivered a new set of CBA proposals covering roster-rule changes, limits on roster churn, and player data transparency. The exchange kept talks moving but underscored how far apart the sides remain on core economics with the agreement expiring December 1, 2026.

headline: MLB formally proposes first salary cap since 1994: $245.3M cap, $171.2M floor
summary: MLB delivered a landmark CBA proposal calling for a hard salary cap of $245.3 million and a floor of $171.2 million starting in 2027, alongside a 50/50 revenue split, centralized television revenue, a minimum-salary jump from $780,000 to $1 million, and a pre-arbitration bonus pool rising to $65 million. The MLBPA immediately blasted the plan as an attempt to 'reduce player compensation by billions of dollars,' making a December lockout appear all but certain.

headline: MLB proposes sweeping draft overhaul ending high school eligibility
summary: As part of CBA negotiations, MLB proposed a dramatic reworking of amateur player acquisition, including eliminating draft eligibility for high school players, shrinking the draft, and cutting signing-bonus negotiations. The union sharply opposed the framework, setting up the amateur entry system as a major battleground alongside the salary cap ahead of the CBA's December 1 expiration.
